about: The money / permission rules of the counter, ONE table for the three places that apply them (the owner, 2026-11-12: 'make main on the same page for rules as the Pi and terminal').

The Pi enforces them (the source of truth: agent contract 2.10 Permissions, 2.10n, 2.10s, 2.10x); main stores every money event and FLAGS what the Pi would not have allowed (main contract 2.5zd); the terminal pre-checks them so the cashier is asked for a manager before the Pi has to say so.

Canonical copy: quicc-ops contract/money-rules.json. Byte copies (scripts/sync-money-rules.sh; the gate's money-rules-check step fails while they differ): main/backend/internal/domain/order/testdata/money-rules.json, agent/internal/domain/terminal/testdata/money-rules.json, terminal/test/fixtures/money-rules.json. Each module's test reads its copy: main TestMoneyRules (domain/order + domain/staff), the Pi TestMoneyRules (domain/terminal + application/terminal), the terminal test/money_rules_test.dart.
Answers: 'allow' | {manager: <action>, limit, requested} (the Pi's 403 manager_required) | {refused: <code>} (the Pi's 4xx, nothing stored).

main: the flags main stores on the money event as the Pi sends it when nobody approved it (approved_by empty); main_if_approved: the flags when a manager's approval rides it (default []); main null = main never sees it / has nothing to check (the Pi refuses it before any event).

Money: cents, positive; a payment's refund: true marks a refund (main's wire makes it negative with its tip folded in). by = who took / gave it (a key of people); approved = a manager's PIN / approval rode it.

people: what main stores (role + their own limits) and the effective limits main computes and sends to the Pi (effective_limits; null = unlimited). A manager is always unlimited (their own limits are ignored, the Pi's rule). 'uma' is a cashier main sends effective_limits null for ('anyone main made unlimited', agent 2.10): Store > Staff can't make one today (main_makes false), the rule is kept so the three agree if it ever does.

2026-11-12 (the owner, 'online orders = called-in orders'): a refund on an earlier day's order (not carried) is allowed with a manager (R24, R25, R33-R36: a cashier gets {manager: refund_earlier_day}; the refund lands in today's batch, drawer and Z); a tip is card only (section tips: a tip on a cash or comp payment is refused for anyone: tip_card_only when the payment is taken, not_tippable when set afterwards; main flags cash_tip if one arrives). The over-comp refusal (R14) and 'managers have no limits' stay.

tips: each case is one payment taken with its tip (payment.tip), or with tip_after true a tip set afterwards on that payment (payment = the payment tipped, tip = the tip set); pi / main as in the other sections.

callcenter (CALLCENTER-PLAN.md, agent contract 2.10ab; 2026-11-12): the role `callcenter` (person 'cece': effective 0 / 0, never unlimited, their own limits ignored) works only through main's relay to the Pi, never on a store terminal. Each row is one thing the call-center app could send: action = what (the Pi's runner TestMoneyRulesCallcenter places a real order and tries it), pi = 'allow' | {refused: not_allowed_for_callcenter, what} (the Pi's 403, before any money or print) | {refused: paid_locked} / {refused: out_of_area} (the Pi's 409s). main never stores a refused one (no main flags); the terminal app never logs this role in (its runner skips the section).

2026-11-12 evening (the owner): a comp, and a void of an order that was sent to the kitchen, are a manager's. comps: a cashier or a driver gets {manager: comp} (C01, C03, P04, P06); a manager or anyone main made unlimited comps alone; reversing a comp stays free (R12, R13, R32). voids: by voids (what: order = Void, waste = Void waste, line = a kitchen change that takes a sent line off and leaves the check smaller, cents = the order's total or how much the check goes down by) -> a cashier or a driver gets {manager: void} with requested = cents; main flags an order.void nobody approved by someone with limits: void_needs_manager (main null = it has nothing to check: a removed line reaches main only as order.changed). An order not sent yet never reaches the Pi (the terminal's Cancel / Wipe is free). The manager rule is the store seats' (terminals): the call center cancels its own unpaid orders and takes lines off unpaid orders without a manager, as its K rows say (V08, V09; paid lines stay locked, it never comps).

tender_voids (batch C, the owner 2026-11-14, agent contract 2.10al): Cash Out's Void on one tender (POST /api/terminal/checks/{id}/tenders/{tid}/void). ANY cashier, no manager, whatever the tender or amount; never counted against a cashier's refund limit (a refunds rule reading an order whose payments hold a void of kind tender_void leaves it out: TV13). order = the order's payments, void = the index of the tender voided; a refund row (TV13) = a later refund on that order by the rules of section refunds. Refused for everyone: a driver (driver_not_allowed), the call center (not_allowed_for_callcenter), an earlier batch (not_payable), a payment that is a refund or a tip added afterwards (not_voidable_tender), a tender a Square refund already gave money back on (tender_refunded). main: what main stores on the void's order.payment (kind tender_void): nothing; main's runner does not read this section yet (main to learn kind tender_void).

mod_prices (batch A, the owner 2026-11-14 #11; agent contract 2.10an): a mod's price (a cart option's price_cents) set at the counter. Any cashier or manager, up or down, to $0 too, no PIN, never a comp, no drop limit; a driver lowering one needs a manager ({manager: mod_price, limit 0, requested = the cents lowered}); raising is free. main null (main sees only the order lines). Run by the Pi's TestMoneyRulesModPrices (application/terminal) and the terminal's test/money_rules_test.dart.
